title: Ada and the Crown
premise: Casper Coldharbour has spent nine years hiding in the Stillvale, the one place in the world where magic cannot follow, believing she fled her hedge-witch master to escape power rather than to escape herself. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Casper learns she is the last heir of the Covenant that once bound the magical realms to the mortal one—and that the Stillvale's magiclessness is not a refuge but a wound she unknowingly made when she ran. Hunted by the Crown's truth-binders, tempted by a fallen queen who offers belonging at the price of lies, Casper must choose between the loyalty she owes her old master and the truth of what he did to her, and finally reforge the Covenant with her own name spoken aloud. In the end she does not restore the old order but writes a new one, giving the realms a covenant built on consent rather than fear, and discovers that the child she saved is the future she has chosen.
about_author: Oscar Brightwater is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping coastlines that no longer exist, and who now maps imaginary ones instead. They live in a house full of dictionaries for languages nobody speaks, which they insist are for research.

chapters.title: The Valley That Refuses
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Establish the Stillvale, where spells die at the border stones, and Casper's careful, magic-free life mending charms she cannot cast. A knocking at the door at dusk reveals a child, mud-caked and silent, whose words—when they come—are in no living tongue. Emotional beat: the dread of a hidden life cracking open.

chapters.title: A Language Older Than Kings
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Using her master's forbidden lexicon, she identifies the child's speech as Covenant-tongue, dead for three centuries. The child's words are a summons, and each phrase Casper translates leaves a faint mark on her own skin. Emotional beat: reluctant fascination curdling into fear as the marks spell her true name.

chapters.title: What the Master Buried
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, with a flashback to her apprenticeship. She returns to her old master Aldous's cottage for answers and finds it ransacked, his grimoire missing, and a truth-binder's seal on the door. A memory surfaces: Aldous carving the Stillvale's silence into being, using her as the anchor. Emotional beat: betrayal recontextualized—her refuge is her prison.

chapters.title: The Queen of Ashes
chapters.summary: Introduce Vessandra, the fallen queen of the near realm, in her POV. She has spent centuries whispering through cracks in the Covenant, and the child's arrival means the last heir is awake. She sends her charming, hollow-eyed envoy Tam to Casper with an offer of sanctuary and belonging. Emotional beat: seductive menace; power as a warm hand on a cold neck.

chapters.title: Truth-Binders at the Ford
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The Crown's truth-binders catch up to them at the river ford, led by the inquisitor Serah Dane, who offers Casper a bargain: surrender the child and her own crimes will be forgotten. Casper flees across the border stones, and magic—her magic—floods back for the first time in nine years. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration entwined; power returning like blood to a numb limb.

chapters.title: The Cost of the First Spell
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. On the road, Casper casts her first real spell and the child speaks her first full sentence: the Covenant is failing, and every day it frays, a realm dies. Casper's spells work but take memories as payment, and she begins forgetting the Stillvale—her mother's face, Aldous's kindness, her own reasons for running. Emotional beat: grief as tuition; power's price made personal.

chapters.title: Tam's Kindness
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The envoy genuinely grows fond of Casper and the child, which complicates his orders to deliver them to Vessandra. He shows Casper a memory of what the old Covenant actually was: a leash, with mortals at the collar's end. Emotional beat: loyalty to a person versus loyalty to a cause; the reader's sympathies split.

chapters.title: The Throne of Whispered Names
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Captured and brought before Vessandra, Casper is offered the truth: Aldous did not merely use her—he made her, a covenant-anchor in human shape, and Vessandra offers to unmake that, freeing her entirely, if Casper will hand over the child. Casper nearly accepts. Emotional beat: the temptation of a painless lie; belonging offered as a bargain.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Climax. Casper's POV. At the shattered Covenant-stone, Casper refuses both Vessandra's lie and Serah Dane's bargain, and instead speaks her true name—the one Aldous carved away—claiming the anchor role on her own terms. Tam turns against his queen at the critical moment; Serah Dane, bound by her own truth-oaths, must witness rather than stop it. The Covenant is reforged, but Casper pours her stolen memories into it as mortar. Emotional beat: self-acceptance as an act of power; the cost paid knowingly.

chapters.title: A New Wording
chapters.summary: Resolution, shifting between Casper's and the child's POV. The Stillvale's silence lifts; Aldous, freed from his centuries-long binding, returns to find his apprentice his equal and his judge. Casper drafts the Covenant's new first clause—consent, spoken aloud—and the child, revealed as the first born under the new wording, speaks it fluently. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted; a quiet ending that opens outward.
